analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md, with no code, key-handling, attestation or crypto changes. The supplied units are BASE text, lines 1-415 and 416-801. The changed ranges are line 3 (date bump), the GLM5Next video paragraph around base lines 810-811 and 827, and additions at head lines 876-895 and 1732-1751. Those head additions fall outside the supplied excerpts and are only partly visible in the truncated patch.

The visible patch changes the documented GLM5Next video behavior. Variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are now indexed at i / nominalFrameRate, as in the reference loader, instead of being refused with a 400. This is a documented behavior change in the media decode path. It touches the media-ingest surface (TB-007, T-050) and the availability surface (T-010, T-029). The bounds the docs still state are the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token cap and the media reservation (GLM5NextVisionBudget). Those bounds do not depend on a constant frame rate, so removing the VFR refusal does not obviously remove a memory control. I cannot confirm from docs alone that the decode path enforces those caps before allocation when the track has variable frame timing. That belongs to the code PR that shipped alongside this doc change, not to this documentation diff.

The documentation does not alter the prefix-cache/T-041 posture. The documented cache behavior is unchanged. Media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture. Super cache scope is the authenticated tenant scope, and the slot emits no cache receipts. No threat-model assumption is invalidated.

Remaining question for integration: verify that the corresponding GLM5Next video decode code bounds frame count, memory and wall-clock for VFR tracks, and that the patched head lines 876-895 and 1732-1751 introduce no new security claims. The excerpts do not show those lines.
